The UK Government published the Digital Inclusion Action Plan: One Year On progress report on 24 March 2026.
The report states that 1.6 million people have no internet connection at all.
The February 2025 Digital Inclusion Action Plan was described as the first UK government digital-inclusion plan for a decade.
The plan identified four areas: digital skills, internet and device access, inclusive online services with offline options, and trusted local support.
The accompanying call for evidence received 800 responses, with a summary published in July 2025.
Government launched an £11.9 million Digital Inclusion Innovation Fund for local projects across the UK.
Age UK support referenced in the report operated in 13 communities across England.
Government reported a multi-department pilot to refurbish and donate end-of-life devices with the Digital Poverty Alliance.
Virgin Media O2's Community Calling programme, delivered with Hubbub, was reported to have helped more than 32,000 people get online with free phones.
The report states that around 1.7 million UK households do not have a laptop, tablet or desktop computer.
Ofcom's March 2023 home-broadband findings combined measurements delivered to customer routers with data from the UK's four largest broadband providers.
Average home-broadband download speed was 69.4 Mbit/s in March 2023, 17% higher year on year.
Eighty-eight per cent of measured lines received a 24-hour average download speed of at least 30 Mbit/s in March 2023, up from 83% a year earlier.
Average upload speed reached 18.4 Mbit/s, an increase of 7.8 Mbit/s or 73% year on year.
During the 8pm-to-10pm peak period, average urban download speed was 70.3 Mbit/s and rural speed was 56.0 Mbit/s; the reported gap was 26%, down from 58% in 2022.
